failure_modes.name: Query_Stagnation
failure_modes.evidence: All three queries ask essentially the same question with only minor rewording: Query 1: 'What were the dates of the Battle of Harlem Heights and the Battle of White Plains during the American Revolutionary War, and how do they relate to the broader New York Campaign of 1776?'; Query 2: 'What were the specific dates and locations of the Battle of Harlem Heights and the Battle of White Plains during the American Revolutionary War's New York campaign?'. Both queries seek the same facts (dates and locations of the two battles) that were already answered in hop 1. The retrieval results are nearly identical across all three hops, returning the same Battle of Harlem Heights and Battle of White Plains passages each time.

failure_modes.name: Repetitive_Output_Loop
failure_modes.evidence: The solver produces nearly identical summaries across hops 1 and 2. Summary 1: 'The claim is partially inaccurate. While it correctly identifies the Battle of White Plains as occurring on October 28, 1776...the Battle of Harlem Heights actually occurred on September 16, 1776, making it chronologically distinct from the Battle of White Plains, which took place over a month later.' Summary 2: 'The claim is inaccurate. While the Battle of White Plains did occur on October 28, 1776...The Battle of Harlem Heights took place on September 16, 1776, in Manhattan's Morningside Heights and Harlem neighborhoods—over a month before White Plains and in a completely different location.' Both summaries restate the same conclusion (two separate battles, different dates and locations) without advancing verification.
